newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SAirRelations profit dips on charges.
newsitem.headline: SAirRelations profit dips on charges.

text.p: SAirRelations, part of the new SAirGroup that includes Swissair , on Wednesday said 1996 net profit fell 17 percent on one-off charges, but it was confident of returning to past growth rates in 1997.

SAirRelations, which includes the expanding Swissotel hotel chain and the world's second largest caterer Gate Gourmet, said 1996 operating profit rose 40 percent to 175 million francs ($119 million) and sales rose 38 percent to 2.6 billion.
However, 44 million francs in provisions for integrating the duty-free business of Britain's Allders International, acquired last year, pushed net profit down to 40 million from 1995's 49 million.

"Next year we are confident our profit curve will again point upwards," chief financial officer Juerg Forster told a news conference, noting net profit had jumped from a mere 2.7 million in 1993 to 1995's 49 million before dipping.

SAirRelations was previously known as Swissair Associated Cos (SAC), but was renamed late in 1996 as part of a restructuring of the Swissair Group to emphasise that it is no longer purely an airline group, but a diversified services group.
Through a series of acquisitions in recent years, SAirGroup has expanded its profitable catering and duty-free business to compensate for the volatile and loss-making airline business.

Last week SAirGroup reported a 1996 net loss of 497 million francs after provisions of 567 million to cover the adjustment to Europe's liberalised skies and writing down the value of its 49.5 percent stake in Belgian partner Sabena SA .
SAirRelations' operating profit last year accounted for 50 percent of SAirGroup's total operating profit, while its sales accounted for around one-third of the group's sales.
Wolfgang Werle, president of SAirRelations, said he was confident of meeting the 1997 sales budget of 3.3 billion francs as Allders was only partially included in the 1996 result.
SAirRelations operates relatively independent from the SAirGroup with more than 90 percent of its sales coming from customers outside the SAirGroup.
This has raised speculation that SAirGroup, headed by the Philippe Bruggisser, could spin off SAirRelations.
Werle, however, strongly denied any such plans, saying: "At the moment nothing like that is being discussed."

Hotel chain Swissotel, which had its best year, boosted its operating profit to 41 million francs from 23 million, benefiting from the economic boom in the U.S., where hotel rooms have become scarce and prices gone up.

Swissotel has put its four hotels in the U.S. up for sale as part of a stategy to reduce capital tied up in properties, but expand the number of hotels under management to around 60 from the current 16.

Airline caterer Gate Gourmet boosted operating profit to 120 million francs from 96 million and expects to continue its recent rash of acquisitions as the worldwide process of concentration is far from over.
"Half of the world seems to be for sale," said Henning Boysen, managing director for Gate Gourmet.

Gate Gourmet, second to Deutsche Lufthansa AG's LSF Skychef, has been expanding outside its traditional European home market, but still has no foothold in the U.S. market, dominated by Dobbs International Services and LSG Skychef.
"Our goal in 1997 is to establish a presence in the U.S.," Boysen said, adding this could take a variety of forms, ranging from cooperation to alliances.
Gate Gourmet has expanded as airlines outsource catering operations to focus on their core business. Airlines also conclude agreements with one caterer to supply their global network.
